summary: Shared change (native check reliability plus one practice-seed environment variable; no gameplay change). Three separate causes made check-card-deselection and check-board-ui fail intermittently: (1) the native checks play real practice matches from a random seed, so the dealt hand card differs per run, and when it needs a target the first click now starts a play draft (issue 952), which the deselection probe was not written for - it now picks a hand card that does not start a draft; (2) the hover probe aimed at a card that was still settling and checked once - it now waits until the card has been still for 12 frames, takes window focus (a tooltip, which carries the preview, is shown only to a focused window), keeps the pointer on the card until the preview opens within a bound, and reports window and pointer state on failure; (3) check-board-ui battle-expanded asserted on an army attachment that some random matches never have at their battle - it now treats that as not ready and uses the existing bounded retry. MatchSession prints PRACTICE_SEED in capture runs and honours L5R_PRACTICE_SEED, so any failure can be replayed exactly.
validation: Measured before and after, repeated runs, full CPU load on every core: deselection battle mode failed 1 of 8 before and passes 12 of 12 after; hover mode failed 1 of 10 idle and 1 of 12 under load before, passes 20 of 20 under load after; battle-expanded failed deterministically for seed 11030758424791007531 (replayed 3 of 3) and passes that seed and 12 of 12 unseeded runs under load after. Full tools/check-card-deselection.sh and tools/check-board-ui.sh pass. Native UI checks are not run in CI.
remaining: Other native checks that fail on main for unrelated reasons are unchanged (action-lock-ui, battle-sequence-ui, support-cards, persistent-home, gameplay-controls). The same random-seed dependence may affect other board and decision captures; the printed seed is the tool for finding it.
